scope: audit the second kit, and catch myself reporting two false greens

catalogSubmission.gateResult: All 1 submitted entry passes: dsh.bundle declared, repo old enough, enough commits.
catalogSubmission.waitingOn: the batch merge queue, not the gate

verifyKitAudit.before: 0/1 rules recognised — the audit only knew vertical-kit's add(level, rule) style
verifyKitAudit.fixed: added findings.push({level, rule}) recognition, including multi-line objects; path argument so one script audits any kit
verifyKitAudit.firstRealRun: 10/26 rules covered in both directions across 5 packages

thirdDeadRule.why: the heading regex required #{1,6}\s+ then non-empty text, so `##` alone — the exact case the rule exists for — was never parsed as a heading
thirdDeadRule.irony: the test written to prove the rule fires proved it could not
thirdDeadRule.npxVerified: `##` alone now reports empty-heading; a clean document still reports nothing

tenOneDirectionalRules.citelint: no clean-document test at all — six rules had never been seen staying silent on a correct citation block

myOwnErrors.error: push loop grepped for 'main -> main|up-to-date', so a blocked commit (nothing to push) reported PUSH OK
myOwnErrors.consequence: I believed a commit had landed when the commit-msg hook had rejected it for a 79-char subject — my own tool, on my own commit, and my own loop hid it
myOwnErrors.fix: check the push exit code, not the output text

myOwnErrors.error: a version bump printed 'was 0.1.3 -> 0.1.4' but package.json on disk was 0.1.1, so the publish failed with 'cannot publish over 0.1.1'
myOwnErrors.consequence: one wasted publish cycle; the printed line was not verified against the file
myOwnErrors.fix: grep the version out of package.json after writing it, before publishing

observation: the audit's value is now measured in two kits: 6 defects in vertical-kit, 1 dead rule plus 10 one-directional rules in verify-kit. It also caught two of my own process errors inside the same session, which is the first time a gate has caught the operator rather than the code.
